design_notes: Rows, costs and days are those of table 6.6. All of them are game values (section 19).
applies_to_scope is the Applies to column as one word. applies_to_categories lists the part categories that hold such hardware; it is a reading of the column, which the design does not spell out.
reveals_failure_modes maps the Reveals column to the failure modes of 8.4. Where no failure mode matches ("loose components", "thermal design faults", "countdown issues"), the reveal is a flag.
Effects with a number in the design: component qualification narrows the uncertainty band by 50%, engine hot-fire adds 1% reliability (stored as +0.01, percentage points).

Effects chosen by the data author because the design shows only a plus sign (game values, to be tuned): vibration test "payload reliability +" = +0.01 reliability on the payload, the same size as the hot-fire bonus; arc-jet test "+heat margin" = +5% heat margin on the tested shield, the size of a Bronze Heat Margin boost.
Qualitative effects left as flags because no effect target fits: "fewer holds" (wet dress rehearsal), "power & thermal +" (thermal-vacuum), "Removes pogo risk if found" (pogo suppression).

The design gives no probability that a test reveals a hidden flaw and no cost for fixing one (6.5: "for time and money"; Appendix A shows a $1 M fix). The Test Failure anomaly card carries the choice.

minigames follows the sentence under the table (MG-03, MG-04, MG-06). MG-03 names the static fire and MG-06 the vibration test in section 10.5. MG-04 Orientation Check names no test ("avionics/sensor integration", reward "parachute & sensor reliability"); it is attached to the software-in-the-loop test (avionics / GNC) and to the drop test (parachutes; 8.4 links the Genesis fact of MG-04 to parachute failure). To be confirmed.
MG-11 Pogo Damper is a flight minigame whose chance rises without the pogo test; it is not a build minigame and is not listed.
No applies_to_categories: "Any part" means every category.
"5% of part cost" has no meaning for options without a cost (the design gives none for RCS, power and most communications options).
"Turbopump flaws" is mapped to engine_shutdown, whose cause in 8.4 is "low-reliability engine, skipped hot-fire".
The design does not say whether "10% of engine cost" is the cost of one engine or of all engines on the stage.
The design gives a cost range of $2–8 M and does not say what sets the price inside it (presumably the size of the stage).
"Plumbing leaks" is mapped to cryogenic_leak (8.4: propellant loss, mitigated by testing). A stage is not one part category; the list names the categories that make up a stage.
No applies_to_categories: the test is run on the whole vehicle.
The +0.01 reliability is chosen by the data author; the design says only "payload reliability +".
The design gives a cost range of $1–3 M and does not say what sets the price inside it.

Only the options with parachutes count: both parachute options of capsule_recovery, Parachute + splashdown of booster_recovery and the three Mars landers (each lands with a parachute). The mandatory parachute recovery of C0 has no part.
The +5% heat margin is chosen by the data author; the design says only "+heat margin".
Skipping this test is the trigger of the Software Bug Found anomaly card (6.8).
The cause of pogo in 8.4 is a "long first stage", so the first-stage tank size is listed beside the engine. The design does not say which tank sizes count as long.
